header: ES 412 OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND SAFETY II – FINAL EXAM – JUNE 2026
instructions: This examination is comprised of 25 multiple-choice questions. Each question is followed by four possible answers, of which only one is correct. The maximum time for this examination is 40 minutes.
notes: Sınavın yalnızca S12-S21 fotoğrafları mevcut; S1-11 ve S22-25 yok.
S16-17 için 5x5 risk matrisi şekli kırpıldı (img/es412-final-2026-06/q16.jpg).
S18-21 senaryo soruları; senaryo metni 'passage' olarak ayrıldı. Fotoğraflar eğik/çekim kalitesi orta; metin okunabilir.

items.text: Which statement about asbestos is correct?

options.t: The health effects of asbestos exposure usually appear immediately after contact.
Asbestos fibers are too large to reach the lungs.
Prolonged inhalation of asbestos fibers can cause serious and fatal illnesses, including asbestosis and lung cancer.
Asbestos is used exclusively in the chemical industry.

items.text: What is the most critical safety hazard associated with flickering light around moving machinery?

options.t: Flickering light may make a machine appear to be moving slower than it actually is or appear to have stopped when it has not.
Flickering light distorts workers' color perception, leading to material defects.
Flickering light causes only headaches and eye fatigue, posing no safety risk.
Flickering light adversely affects workers' hearing.

items.text: Which statement about the correct positioning of portable straight or extension ladders is correct?

options.t: The horizontal distance from the base to the support point should be one-quarter of the working length of the ladder.
The preferred angle is 45 degrees from horizontal.
The top of the ladder should extend 50 cm above the upper surface.
The steeper the ladder angle, the safer the ladder.

items.text: What is the key difference between a Preliminary Hazard Analysis (PHA) and a Preliminary Hazard List (PHL)?

options.t: The PHL ranks hazardous events by severity, while the PHA only lists them.
The PHA identifies hazards, ranks them by severity, and provides recommendations; the PHL is only a list of potential hazards.
PHA is another name for Fault Tree Analysis (FTA).
A PHL requires more technical expertise than a PHA.

items.text: A worker operates a machine with a moderate chance (possible, score = 3) of mechanical failure leading to severe injury (critical, score = 4). According to a standard 5×5 risk matrix, how should this risk be classified?

options.t: Low risk – no immediate action needed
Medium risk – monitor with periodic review
High risk – requires prompt corrective action
Extreme risk – work must be stopped immediately

items.text: A chemical spill in a laboratory has a low likelihood (2: Unlikely), if it happens, the consequences would be catastrophic (5: multiple fatalities possible). Based on the 5×5 risk matrix provided, how should this risk be classified?

options.t: Low risk – tolerable without new measures
Medium risk – review and monitor periodically
High risk – corrective action required soon
Extreme risk – immediate action required, stop work until resolved

items.passage: 18. SCENARIO — Workers in a metal-stamping plant are exposed to continuous noise levels of 102 dB(A). Measurements confirm all workers exceed the maximum action limit. The plant manager lists the following options under consideration:

items.text: Rank these four options (i–iv) correctly from HIGHEST to LOWEST in the hierarchy of control measures.
list: (i) Replace the old pneumatic stamping presses with quieter electric servo-presses (78 dB).
(ii) Build acoustic enclosures around each press.
(iii) Rotate workers between noisy and quiet areas every two hours.
(iv) Provide each worker with earmuffs rated NRR 29.

options.t: (iv) → (iii) → (ii) → (i)
(i) → (ii) → (iii) → (iv)
(ii) → (i) → (iv) → (iii)
(iii) → (i) → (ii) → (iv)

items.passage: 19. SCENARIO — An OHS manager at a chemical plant has completed a Preliminary Hazard Analysis (PHA) and identified a high-risk scenario: a pressurized solvent storage tank could rupture, causing fire and explosion. The risk score is rated CRITICAL (highest severity × high probability). The manager now proposes the following corrective actions:

items.text: According to the hierarchy of control measures and the ALARP principle, which action should be PRIORITISED first?
list: (i) Demolish the above-ground tank and store the solvent in sealed underground tanks with automatic leak detection.
(ii) Reduce the maximum fill volume to 60% of tank capacity.
(iii) Require all workers within 50 m of the tank to wear flame-resistant coveralls and face shields.
(iv) Conduct weekly visual inspections of the tank and pressure gauges.

options.t: Option (iii) – flame-resistant PPE for nearby workers
Option (iv) – weekly visual inspections
Option (ii) – limiting fill volume to 60%
Option (i) – replacing the above-ground tank with a sealed underground system

items.passage: 20. SCENARIO — A forestry company cannot afford to replace its fleet of chainsaws immediately. The OHS manager has a budget to implement ONE additional control measure on top of the existing anti-vibration gloves already in use.

items.text: Which single measure would represent the greatest IMPROVEMENT in the hierarchy level (i.e., moving to a higher control level) compared to gloves alone?

options.t: Switch from standard chainsaws to anti-vibration chainsaws with rubber-isolated handles.
Provide workers with thicker anti-vibration gloves with a higher attenuation rating.
Display warning posters reminding workers to take breaks.
Conduct annual hand-arm vibration health surveillance for all workers.

items.passage: 21. SCENARIO — Workers at a food processing facility frequently slip on wet floors near washing stations. Incident records show 12 same-level fall accidents in the past year. The floors are smooth ceramic tiles. Water accumulates from continuous rinsing operations throughout the shift. Currently, workers are warned with wet-floor signs.

items.text: The facilities manager proposes four options. Which option is HIGHEST in the hierarchy of control measures?

options.t: Replace the smooth ceramic floor tiles with anti-slip textured flooring throughout the washing station area.
Post additional wet-floor warning signs and hold a toolbox talk to remind workers to walk carefully.
Require all workers in the wet area to wear safety footwear with slip-resistant soles (rated SRA/SRB).
Implement a cleaning schedule requiring the floor to be mopped and dried every 30 minutes.
